# Verification record

## SDK 0.1.6 PlayStation SPU candidate — 2026-10-28

This is an unpublished local candidate. SDK metadata and CMake identify 0.1.6; no tag, push, remote CI run or release is claimed. Consumers record the candidate source archive hash, base commit and changed paths explicitly. Historical records below retain their original dates and scope.

- All 17 files imported from the reference application's `native/ps1/` are byte-identical under `vendor/mame-ps1-spu/`. This includes all adapted C++/headers, the BSD-3-Clause license and the five pristine MAME sources, immutable revision and SHA-256 list. The source audit covers **324 snapshot records**, the unchanged **24 generic chip IDs / 29 chip WASM recipes / two application-audio modules / two JavaScript references**, and one separate `ps1_spu` instrument. The aggregate selector now exposes **32 recipes**.
- The C++17 target `tetorica::ps1_spu` and C-compatible `<tetorica/ps1_spu.h>` expose the original synchronous `ps1_spu_*` ABI. An independently extracted source archive built all **24 static libraries** and **51 executables**, then passed **30/30 CTest entries** from 29 fixture executables. All **22 offline WAV examples** passed finite/nonzero/unclipped PCM16 stereo audits: the original PS1 waveform/melody has 132,300 frames at 44,100 Hz; the earlier 21 examples retain 144,000 frames at 48 kHz. Both JavaScript references retain their 10 passing smoke checks.
- The SPU fixture checks register/RAM/render guards, all 24 voices, high key-mask bank, fixed stereo gain, ADSR release, Room reverb tail, reset/RAM retention, exact block partitions and independent instances. It does not claim allocation-free arbitrary sample/cache activity, hardware-exact interpolation/envelopes/reverb, CPU/PSF playback or CD streaming.
- Emscripten **6.0.6** rebuilt the descriptor and WASM **byte-identically** to the reference application's generated outputs. The actual WASM smoke rendered **311,605 frames**. In the tested dry and Room-reverb 24-voice scenarios, **98,828 interleaved Native/WASM samples matched exactly**, maximum absolute error **0** (acceptance tolerance 1e-6). This establishes agreement between these model builds, not analog or hardware equivalence. No human listening test was performed.
- All **101 Python release/audit regression tests** passed. Instrument-specific cases reject missing/duplicate/stale catalogs, generic-chip claims, wrong aliases/headers, absent/changed provenance and parity requests without a selected SPU artifact. Release CMake File API tests require the SPU fixture/example in single- and multi-configuration layouts, including Windows `.exe` paths. `actionlint` and `git diff --check` passed.
- CI is configured for the existing five Native platforms and a sixth WASM job for `ps1_spu`; that job compiles and compares supplied and source-isolated rebuilt SPU outputs with `--ps1-native-parity`. These configured jobs have not been run remotely as part of this local candidate work.


## Unreleased CD-DA and MSM5205 aggregation — 2026-10-28

This is local SDK source aggregation and validation, with the existing 0.1.5 candidate metadata retained. No SDK version tag, remote CI run, published archive or consuming application's fixed SDK pin is changed by this work. Historical records below retain their original dates and scope.

- The original CD-DA and MSM5205 C11 cores, headers and WASM bridges are included without synthesis changes in the two `vendor/tetorica-*` component directories and `wasm/{cdda,msm5205}_wasm.c`. Public C forwarders expose `tetorica::cdda` / `tetorica::msm5205` and the unchanged `cdda_pcm_*` / `msm5205_pcm_*` ABIs. Source audits cover **306 snapshot records**, 24 chip IDs, 29 sound-chip WASM artifacts, two separate `applicationAudio` modules and both JavaScript references. The aggregate build selector exposes 31 recipes. All **88 Python audit/release regression tests** passed, including rejection of parity requests without a supplied or rebuilt application-audio module.
- An independently extracted source archive built all **23 Native static libraries** and **49 executables**: 28 fixtures and 21 WAV examples. Release CTest passed **29/29 entries**. All **21 WAV examples** rendered 144,000 frames of 48 kHz stereo PCM16, with finite, nonzero output and no clipping. The two unchanged JavaScript references passed their **10 smoke checks**. These stages required no Tauri, npm dependency, sibling checkout, machine runtime or audio device.
- The three new Native CTest entries also passed from a standalone `cmake -S native` Release build. Two C11 consumers check the CD-DA/MSM5205 source/control contracts; a C++14 consumer links both with the real HuC6280 target.
- Local Emscripten builds produced both descriptor/raw-WASM pairs byte-identically to the corresponding main application files. Each module has no host imports, fixed 128 KiB linear memory and at most 128 stereo output frames per bridge call. Both archived pairs and both pairs rebuilt from the independently extracted sources passed their standalone Node ABI smokes.
- Independently compiled C11 cores and C++14 hosts matched both archived and isolated-source rebuilt WASM exactly: CD-DA at 8/44.1/48/384 kHz; MSM5205 raw behavior and the separate PCE driver at 44.1/48 kHz, including all 16 rate register values, an alternate clock and exact render partitions. The raw decoder oracle is the unchanged Analyzer JavaScript reference. Maximum Native/WASM PCM difference was zero in the tested cases; this establishes model agreement, not analog/hardware equivalence.
- The new original three-source WAV example auditions HuC6280, MSM5205 and CD-DA before their sum. Measured solo RMS values were approximately 0.05679, 0.07070 and 0.05656; the combined peak was approximately 0.30832, with no clipping and an exactly silent final **0.2 seconds**. The explicit 0.5 master scalar applies once. No human listening test is claimed.

The outer archive-checker invocation exited with status 1 when its final Emscripten rebuild encountered a toolchain-cache `PermissionError`. The failed build subprocess was retried with the required cache access; both isolated-source builds, ABI smokes and Native parity checks then completed successfully as separate stages, without a source-code change. The completed stages above are not a claim that the original outer invocation returned success.

The configured five-platform Native matrix and five selected WASM jobs do not establish remote platform success for these additions. No new SDK release or consumer-pin update is claimed.

## POKEY and dual POKEY development validation — 2026-10-27

This is local macOS development validation. `sdk.json` remains `0.1.4`; these local verification archives are not a new published `v0.1.4` release. The main application's fixed SDK 0.1.4 snapshot, runtime, Mixer and generated assets remain unchanged.

- Source checks pass for **24 SDK chip IDs, 29 WASM recipes, two JavaScript references and 292 imported-file records**. Only the explicitly BSD-3-Clause-labeled libvgm `pokey.c` at `61b62d64455e039de2a1d01498afa9e9b5f1cb88` is retained as upstream POKEY source. Unmarked integration/helper files are omitted; both builds compile the documented standalone adaptation.
- The actual Release POKEY fixture passed **3,055,137 checks**, including raw volume-only gain/clipping, real read-side I/O, immediate monitor mute with retained phase, cold reset, multiple clocks/rates, exact render partitions and independent dual-chip lifetimes. It observed zero C++ `new`/`new[]` allocations over 2,048 tested hot render/control blocks; direct C `malloc` was not instrumented. A separate AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer build passed the same fixture.
- An independently extracted source ZIP built all **21 Native libraries**, passed **26 CTest entries** from 25 fixture executables, and rendered/validated all **20 original WAV examples**. The two JavaScript references passed their 10 smoke checks without npm, a sibling checkout, an external ROM/sample or an audio device.

Both released and rebuilt JS/WASM passed the standalone ABI smoke over **1,524,102 frames each**, covering all four physical voices, three clocks/rates, exact partitions and two handles sharing one module heap. Their WASM SHA-256 was `99871b375b6022435684c902bfffeda386e026332c3e12f7bc8dfcaddc9a6f22`.
- Both archive variants passed the actual Native/WASM comparison: **57 cases in two render layouts, 235,091 compared stereo frames, 32 independently specified checks and maximum difference zero per variant**. The comparison includes raw DAC/divider expectations and one chip's continuation while the other is muted, reset or destroyed. This establishes backend agreement for the tested scope, not equivalence to Atari hardware.
- The original dual-POKEY example generated 144,000 frames of 48 kHz PCM16. Default 0.5/0.5 centered mono had equal channel peaks `0.14178466796875` and no differing stereo frames. Explicit `--stereo` produced peaks `0.08795166015625` / `0.1187744140625` and 143,989 differing frames. Its DC blocker and file fades apply only to listening output; raw library PCM remains positive mono with the legacy `/32768` scaling.
- All **70 Python audit/release tests** passed, including missing/unbuilt POKEY artifacts and discovered `.exe` paths under single- and multi-configuration CMake layouts. The POKEY WASM CI job now uses `--pokey-native-parity` to build only the audited extracted fixture and compare it with both the archived and independently rebuilt WASM. The five-platform Native matrix and three WASM jobs are configured; no new remote CI run, tag or release is claimed here.

The final local archive was repackaged after documentation updates and re-audited. Its non-document source/build/test payload is byte-identical to the archive that passed the extracted POKEY rebuild and parity checks. Existing historical records below retain their original release/platform scope.

## Source and release audits

`scripts/check_sdk.py` verifies 22 Playground chip IDs, 27 WASM recipes, two separate JavaScript reference engines, three pinned upstream ADPCM source snapshots, and their SHA-256 digests and source/license references. Imported-source amendments, include-path adaptations and documentation updates are recorded alongside the original digests in the provenance inventory. Release-audit regression tests cover these checks.

Source and WASM archives were extracted outside the original repositories. The audits checked complete manifest coverage, hashes and byte sizes, safe relative paths, source catalogs, and the identity of the source ZIP embedded in the WASM release. CMake File API and compiler-command records confirmed that project sources and include paths stayed within the extracted SDK and its build directory.

```sh
python3 scripts/check_sdk.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
python3 scripts/package_release.py --out-dir releases --wasm-dir build/verified-wasm
python3 tests/check_standalone_release.py \
  --source-zip releases/tetorica-soundchip-native-0.1.0-sources.zip \
  --wasm-zip releases/tetorica-soundchip-native-0.1.0-wasm.zip \
  --build-wasm ym2612
```

These checks use installed compilers, Node.js, Python and CMake. They do not download sound-chip sources or another application's checkout. Source and license records preserve the SDK's BSD-3-Clause original-code license and the component exceptions listed in [LICENSES.md](../LICENSES.md).

The amended Native adapter and provider passed another 198-case comparison against the deployed WASM with zero PCM/status/IRQ/read differences.

## Sega PSG and the Genesis WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::segapsg` static target exposes the existing `native_game_gear_*` C ABI through `<tetorica/segapsg.hpp>`. The imported renderer and wrapper bytes are unchanged. The core is now in `vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/` with annotation-only copyright/SPDX headers; `catalog/source_inventory.json` retains its original and current hashes. The fixture's source revision, original hash and additional test coverage are recorded in `native/reference/SOURCES.json`.
- Release CMake builds and all three CTest fixtures passed. The PSG fixture covers three tones, all eight noise modes, continuation latches, Game Gear stereo routing, independent instances, mute/unmute phase, retained Stop, reset, clock limits and observational snapshots. Rendering and controls observed zero C++ `new`/`delete` calls.
- Comparison of the SDK-built Release fixture against the shipped PSG Worklet/WASM passed 66 cases at 44,100, 48,000 and 96,000 Hz: 436,224 stereo frames with zero PCM differences. Cases include all 256 stereo masks, tone-three noise coupling, attenuation, slow-clock average/hold and retained Stop. This extra comparison uses `scripts/check_native_game_gear.mjs` in the original application checkout, which is not a package build dependency.
- `tetorica_genesis_wav` links the SDK YM2612 and Sega PSG libraries to render a three-second, 48 kHz PCM16 stereo example from synthetic notes and noise. It uses explicit chip clocks and fixed demo mix gains; it does not apply the Playground's Mixer presets. The archive checker requires the executable, runs it into the isolated build directory and checks WAV format, complete PCM payload, nonzero samples in both channels and output headroom.
- An independently extracted source ZIP built all three libraries, all three fixtures and the combined example in Release mode. CTest passed 3/3. The example wrote 144,000 stereo frames; both channel peaks were approximately 0.104, without clipping. The ten JavaScript reference checks and existing YM2612 WASM ABI smoke also passed against the extracted releases.
- All 50 Python regression tests passed. They require the PSG fixture and example executable, reject missing or unbuilt artifacts and malformed, silent, clipped or truncated WAV output, and retain the Windows/single-/multi-configuration path checks. Source validation checked 255 snapshot records.

Sega PSG alone does not provide Genesis FM or the Master System's optional YM2413. Hosts use stereo mask `0xff` for centered Genesis/Master System output and may select individual Game Gear routes. The standalone PSG target opens no audio device and includes no host scheduler or real-time deadline guarantee. Existing WASM recipes and the YM2612-only compiled WASM release remain unchanged by this Native addition.

## YM2413 and the Master System WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::ym2413` static target and public `<tetorica/ym2413.hpp>` header expose the existing `native_ym2413_*` C ABI. ADPCM/PCM definitions are included as separate archive members to satisfy the unchanged full OPL provider; this does not establish standalone SDK support for the other OPL chips.
- Release CMake builds and CTest passed 4/4. The OPLL-only fixture covers all nine melodic channels, sixteen instrument selections including the shared user patch, rhythm gates and retained levels, reads/observations, Stop/reset, deferred audition, independent instances and cancellation across shared rhythm channels. Rendering and controls observed zero C++ `new`/`delete` calls.
- Comparison against the shipped YM2413 Worklet/WASM passed 558 cases at 44,100, 48,000 and 96,000 Hz: 2,285,568 stereo frames with zero PCM, register, clock, status, IRQ or read-port differences. The additional comparison uses the original application's `scripts/check_native_extra_ym2413.mjs` with the SDK-built fixture; that checkout is not a source-package build dependency.

It uses built-in piano, light rhythm percussion and PSG tones, with hardware pitch equations and fixed demo mix gains. The checker runs both WAV examples in the isolated build directory and validates format, payload, nonzero output on both channels and headroom.

The Master System example's channel peaks were approximately 0.035. The ten JavaScript reference checks and existing YM2612 WASM ABI smoke also passed against the extracted releases.
- All 51 Python regression tests passed, including missing/unbuilt YM2413 and Master System example artifacts and rejection of a silent second example. Source validation checked 258 snapshot records. The final source/WASM archives retained matching manifests, provenance and the exact embedded companion source ZIP.

YM2413 provides nine melodic channels, or six melodic channels plus five rhythm voices sharing physical channels 6–8. It is mono and is sent to both output channels. The Master System-style example keeps PSG stereo at `0xff`; it is not a console emulator. This Native addition retains the existing YM2612-only compiled WASM release and does not rebuild unchanged WASM inputs.

## YM2608 and the PC-98 OPNA WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::ym2608` static target and public `<tetorica/ym2608.hpp>` header expose the existing `native_ym2608_*` C ABI, including primary and additional constructors. They reuse the Native OPN provider and unchanged SSG/ADPCM dependencies. The adapter amendment removes its redundant local `keyonoff` template instantiation and updates its ownership comment, matching Tauri revision `83bfba8cbbc272a02279aba250b13e4c0f6ca57b`. Vendor DSP and the exported ABI are retained.
- Each handle reserves 8 KiB of rhythm ROM and 2 MiB of ADPCM-B RAM at creation. Transfers and RAM copies check their complete ranges and copy the bytes; the host need not retain upload buffers. Both profiles retain ROM/RAM, clock and source mute across reset and Stop. `clear_memory()` clears RAM only. State snapshots inspect status without consuming CPU data reads or propagating pending ADPCM status/IRQ effects; explicit raw reads retain their hardware side effects.
- Release CMake builds and CTest passed 7/7 with examples disabled. The default YM2608 self-test exercises both constructor profiles: all six FM channels and stereo gates, isolated instances, memory bounds/copy ownership/rejected-write rollback, retained ROM/RAM and controls, timers/CSM, raw CPU memory transfers, observational ADPCM EOS/IRQ state, cancellation and the exact reset-history distinction at a low clock. Audited rendering and control paths observed zero C++ `new`/`delete` calls.
- Comparison against the shipped WASM passed 30 primary-profile PCM cases and 184,320 stereo frames, plus 252 additional-profile cases and 1,585,152 stereo frames comparing PCM, status, IRQ and four raw ports. All ran at 44,100, 48,000 and 96,000 Hz with maximum difference zero: 282 cases and 1,769,472 stereo frames in total. The optional application-level checks use `scripts/check_native_ym2608.mjs`, `scripts/check_native_extra_ym2608.mjs`, the deployed WASM and that checkout's rhythm-ROM reference bytes with the SDK-built fixture. That application checkout and ROM file are not package build dependencies or inputs to the new synthetic WAV example.

## YM2610 / YM2610B and the NeoGeo WAV example

- The common `tetorica_native_ym2610` static library exposes `tetorica::ym2610` and `tetorica::ym2610b` aliases, with public `<tetorica/ym2610.hpp>` and `<tetorica/ym2610b.hpp>` forwarders to the existing `native_ym2610b_*` C ABI. The constructor selects an immutable variant: `0` enables four physical FM slots (zero-based 1/2/4/5); `1` enables all six. Choosing an alias or header does not select the variant. The convenience `create_extra()` retains its four-FM default. Both variants reuse the existing Native OPN provider and unchanged SSG/ADPCM dependencies; they are not two copies of the implementation. The adapter amendment removes its redundant local `keyonoff` template instantiation and adds an ownership comment, carrying the Tauri provider fix at `83bfba8cbbc272a02279aba250b13e4c0f6ca57b` without changing vendor DSP or the exported ABI.
- Primary handles own two dense, initially zero 16 MiB ROM banks. Successful uploads synchronously copy bytes. Additional handles instead borrow immutable 64 KiB pages in each bank's 16 MiB address space; a nonempty `load_rom()` is rejected. The host prepares pages outside rendering, serializes publication, and keeps current/retired pages alive until every reader is finished. Replacing, clearing or destroying a handle does not free those caller-owned pages. Unmapped pages read as zero. This SDK does not import the application's retirement queue or shared memory budget.
- Both profiles retain their ROM banks/pages, clock and source mute across Stop/reset; both clear outer held PCM and output-rate remainder on reset. Primary `clear_rom()` zeros its selected bank, while the additional profile unpublishes that bank's pointers. Copies and transfers validate complete ranges. YM2610 status reads are observational, unlike YM2608 extended-status IRQ propagation; neither a Native snapshot nor a ROM copy is a transferable WASM save state.
- Release builds and CTest passed 8/8 with examples disabled and from an independently extracted source ZIP with examples enabled. The default YM2610 fixture covers both variants with both constructors, all physical FM slots/stereo gates, SSG and both ADPCM banks, dense copy ownership, sparse page boundaries/publication/replacement, unmapped reads, rejected-range rollback, independent instances, clock limits, timers/status/IRQ, CSM, deferred audition, retained Stop/reset and foreign-bus continuity. Audited rendering and controls observed zero C++ `new`/`delete` calls.
- Actual deployed WASM comparison passed 72 primary PCM cases and 442,368 stereo frames, plus 504 additional-profile cases and 3,096,576 frames comparing PCM, status, IRQ and four raw ports. Both variants ran at 44,100, 48,000 and 96,000 Hz with maximum difference zero: 576 cases and 3,538,944 stereo frames in total. These optional checks use the original application's `scripts/check_native_ym2610b.mjs` and `scripts/check_native_extra_ym2610.mjs` with the SDK-built fixture and synthetic input data; that checkout is not a package build dependency.

- `tetorica_neogeo_wav` uses one primary four-FM YM2610 at 8 MHz, physical slots 1/2/4/5, three SSG voices and locally encoded ADPCM-A percussion/ADPCM-B pluck data in separate ROM banks. It uses FM divider 144, SSG tone frequency master/(64*period), the OPNB 256-byte ADPCM address units and Delta-N sample pitch, with one fixed postmix export gain. No external game or hardware ROM is used.

## OKIM6258 and the X68000 WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::okim6258` alias links `tetorica_native_okim6258`, with public `<tetorica/okim6258.hpp>` forwarding the existing `native_extra_okim6258_*` C ABI and 28-byte state layout. Clock admission also checks FIFO safety at reset's divider 512; at 8 kHz output the accepted upper clock is 57,344,000 Hz. A rejected high-byte clock commit preserves the previous applied clock and staged buffer. State inspection does not advance playback or transfer a WASM save state.

## RF5C164 and the Mega-CD WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::rf5c164` alias links `tetorica_native_rf5c164`. Public `<tetorica/rf5c164.hpp>` forwards both existing `native_rf5c164_*` and `native_extra_rf5c164_*` ABIs; the primary/extra adapters and pinned vendor core remain byte-identical. Each handle independently owns 64 KiB of RAM and eight PCM voices. Reset retains RAM and clock configuration while clearing voice/bank/output history; clearing RAM is a separate operation.
- Absolute uploads copy bytes into owned RAM without changing the selected CPU bank; banked writes use the existing bitwise-OR bank/window mapping. Start addresses use 256-byte units, loops use byte addresses, and pitch steps have eleven fractional bits. Samples are sign-magnitude, with `0xff` reserved as the loop marker. Primary uploads require a valid caller buffer; the additional API explicitly rejects null pointers for nonempty uploads and provides observational state, position reads and RAM copies.

The additional profile accepts 8,000–384,000 Hz output and 100,000–100,000,000 Hz clocks, with up to eight held canonical contributions for clock averaging. Its independent renderer retains each voice's contribution for source cancellation. Ordinary mask writes retain the reference held output until the next tick; additional `key_off()` / `stop()` remove the selected cached contributions immediately without advancing other voices. The primary ABI has no dedicated Stop or read/snapshot functions.
- Release CMake builds and CTest passed 10/10 with examples disabled. The default RF5C164 fixture tests both ABIs: exact common-operation PCM at three output rates and six clock edits, all voices/pan, RAM copy lifetime and boundaries, banked OR writes versus absolute crossing uploads, loop/double-marker behavior, reset/clear, extra observation and rejected-copy rollback. Primary/extra PCM equality is checked separately by CTest and the consumer; this is not a claim of a primary read/snapshot ABI or full primary WASM state comparison.

They exercised both RF ABIs, compared 4,096 frames exactly and produced identical finite, nonzero output; the previous nine libraries' output energies were unchanged.
- `tetorica_megacd_wav` combines actual YM2612, Sega PSG and primary RF5C164 handles, with a locally generated sign-magnitude waveform copied into RAM and shared by three PCM voices. Positive magnitudes avoid the reserved `0xff`; a marker-filled tail catches multi-byte address steps. Nominal PCM pitch uses `Hz * wave_length * 384 * 2048 / clock`, retaining the core's step and loop-restart quantization. ## OPL family and DOS / MSX-AUDIO WAV examples

- The common `tetorica_native_opl` static library exposes `tetorica::opl`, `tetorica::ym3526`, `tetorica::ym3812`, `tetorica::ymf262` and `tetorica::y8950`. The generic public header forwards both existing `native_opl_*` and `native_extra_opl_*` ABIs; chip headers forward the generic header. Aliases and headers do not choose a chip: constructor kind `0` selects YM3526, `1` YM3812, `2` YMF262 and `3` Y8950, constructing only that kind. The existing complete Native OPL provider and unchanged ADPCM/PCM dependencies are reused. The extra adapter amendment removes eighteen redundant explicit method/helper instantiations and their stale ownership comment, carrying the provider fix from Tauri revision `83bfba8cbbc272a02279aba250b13e4c0f6ca57b`. Primary adapter, vendor DSP and exported ABIs are retained.
- The primary and additional fixtures cover all four kinds: 9/18 physical FM channels, waveform and rhythm behavior, OPL3 four-operator pairs and four output buses, timers/status/IRQ, CSM, Stop/reset, preview/audition, clock limits, observation and independent sources. The additional profile retains per-source output for cancellation and restores its captured power-on state on reset; its public release, host silence and strong Stop controls remain distinct from the primary profile. - Y8950 uses up to 512 caller-owned, writable 4 KiB pages in a 2 MiB address space. Page publication borrows pointers without copying or freeing; the host serializes readers/writers and retains current/retired storage until no reader can use it. They do not advance audio or consume CPU data bytes, but they are not guaranteed IRQ-neutral. Raw CPU data reads have their separate transfer side effects. The fixture's observational PCM tests do not claim universal status/IRQ neutrality.

## NES with optional FDS and the WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::nes` alias links `tetorica_native_nes`, with public `<tetorica/nes.hpp>` forwarding the existing `native_nes_*` ABI and 400-byte state layout. The Native implementation/header and canonical vendor source/header remain unchanged. Only the self-contained Native implementation is compiled; adding the vendor implementation would duplicate its exports. The target uses C++17 and privately applies the original Tauri `-fwrapv`, `-fno-strict-aliasing` and `-ffp-contract=off` options when supported, retaining JavaScript integer/floating-point behavior without changing unrelated targets. The renderer's explicit Apache-2.0 AND MIT notices and source licenses are retained.
- Construction selects immutable base clock and optional FDS, with output rates 8,000–384,000 Hz and finite base clocks 1,600,000–1,900,000 Hz. Base clocks below 1,700,000 select PAL tables; outer integer clock edits retain that regional core and its phase. Each handle owns copied 64 KiB DMC memory and FDS wave/modulation tables; no caller sample storage is borrowed. Raw FDS wave bytes and submitted register shadows are retained even where the write/IO gates reject their synthesis effect; applied fields and six-bit audible wave data are distinct views.
- Legacy APU enable writes, protected `$4015` merges, independent host gates and source Stop keep their separate contracts, including preservation of the DMC final prefetched byte. Global Stop gates the APU and submits FDS halt/zero-gain writes through its IO gate; disabled FDS IO can leave that oscillator active. `stop_channel(5)` deliberately halts it despite disabled IO while preserving the authored IO setting and envelope/wave data. Per-channel DMC Stop clears the current DAC sample while retaining its authored level/decoder state. Stops do not reset nonlinear mixing, filters or outer held PCM; audible tails may remain. Full reset clears DMC RAM, FDS tables, controls and filter/output history while retaining clock, mute and the constructor choices. ## 32X PWM and the combined WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::pwm` alias links `tetorica_native_pwm`, with public `<tetorica/pwm.hpp>` forwarding the existing `native_pwm_*` ABI and 96-byte state layout. The Native wrapper/header and shared header-only `wasm/pwm32x_core.h` retain their bytes. CMake compiles the wrapper once, using C++17 and the original Tauri `-ffp-contract=off` option where supported. The original primary and additional fixtures retain their CLI formats; the additional fixture can separately exercise the same header-only Core without adding public Native configuration setters.
- Each handle owns left/right three-entry FIFOs, routing/timer state and nonzero 64-bit host ownership tags. Overflow drops the oldest word; underflow retains the current output latch. Raw queued words preserve sixteen bits while output uses the low twelve. Native construction fixes duty output/gain 1 and clock 23,011,361 Hz, accepting output rates 1–1,000,000 Hz. Accepted clock edits preserve queue/timer state; rejected edits leave it unchanged. Active control/cycle writes flush the FIFOs and restart their timer while retaining current latches and their ownership. Global Stop clears FIFOs, latches and tags immediately while retaining clock/control/cycle/timer phase; reset clears chip/timer state and tags while retaining clock.
- Tag zero is ordinary primary traffic. Nonzero cancellation removes matching queued words and owned latches while preserving foreign live queue order, latches and PCM. Unused FIFO storage can be zeroed during compaction, so this does not assert byte identity of invalid slots. Ownership is host metadata rather than a synthesis mode, scheduler or transferable save state. State snapshots and `has_tag()` do not advance time; snapshots omit tags and fixed output configuration.
- Release CMake built all fifteen static libraries and CTest passed 18/18 with examples disabled and assertions enabled. The primary fixture extends constructor defaults/bounds, FIFO flags/capacity/word masking, routing, timer reconfiguration, Stop/reset phase, rejected-operation rollback, observations and independent instances. The additional fixture retains exhaustive routing/count/latch-winner checks and adds 64-bit identity, ordinary/unowned traffic, cancellation lifecycle, flush/Stop/reset retention and direct-Core invalid-state rollback. Both fixtures observed zero C++ allocation/free calls in the audited rendering/control paths.
- Primary comparison against synchronous JavaScript passed 57 cases and 466,944 stereo frames at 44,100, 48,000 and 96,000 Hz with maximum PCM difference zero. The original Tauri `scripts/check_native_pwm.mjs` normally compiles its own fixture; this run used a temporary bootstrap-only override for the SDK-built executable and reference root, retaining scenarios/references/assertions. Released slots can be reused unless protected by the host's bit mask. ## SPC700/SPC player and the synthetic-program WAV example

- The standalone `tetorica::spc` target and public `<tetorica/spc.hpp>` expose the existing `native_spc_*` C ABI, 56-byte observational `NativeSpcState` and 16-byte `NativeSpcEvent`. Five production translation units compile: the unchanged Native wrapper, `SNES_SPC.cpp`, `SNES_SPC_misc.cpp`, `SNES_SPC_state.cpp` and accurate `SPC_DSP.cpp`. Actual CMake commands retain C++17 and supported private `-fwrapv`, `-fno-strict-aliasing` and `-ffp-contract=off` flags. No fast DSP, optional output filter or complete Nintendo IPL is added. The core, wrapper and original ABI header retain LGPL-2.1-or-later notices; the new public forwarder uses the SDK's BSD-3-Clause default. Vendor, wrapper, original header and WASM recipe bytes remain unchanged.
- Load copies a valid SPC file into the CPU/DSP and pauses, retaining the mute mask. The host retains its original bytes when it needs rewind or absolute seeks. Control-only seek advances the current emulated CPU position in blocks of at most 16,000 native frames; a freshly loaded core and repeated bounded blocks establish an absolute target. A core that has rendered audio already includes source lookahead. Load/seek preparation must stay outside the installed rendering core; the SDK supplies no handoff queue. Failed load/seek operations can latch an error until successful reload, rather than providing transactional rollback of all previous state.
- Synthesis remains fixed at 32 kHz with 128-native-frame source blocks, two-frame prefetch and retained integer-phase interpolation to 8–384 kHz output. Pause freezes output and resumes cached audio. Mute changes future source synthesis, preserving CPU/voice progression; cached PCM and echo can remain audible. CPU-rendered frames and listener-position counters intentionally differ because of lookahead. The API does not apply metadata-based duration/fade or detect a musical end automatically.
- State and DSP-register reads do not advance the player. Analysis snapshots need an initialized caller-owned buffer of at least `0x10200` bytes; RAM and DSP ranges are `[0x100,0x10100)` and `[0x10100,0x10180)`. The function writes analysis fields without initializing a complete SPC header and does not capture a seamless CPU/DSP/resampler checkpoint. Observer storage is a fixed per-core allocation with capacity 16–8192; callers exclude mutation while reading/draining it. Event count clearing and saturated overflow-count taking are separate operations. Event clocks include source-buffer lookahead. These contracts and the copied/borrowed lifetimes are documented in the Native guide.
- Release CMake built all eighteen libraries and CTest passed 22/22 from twenty-one fixture executables. The imported SPC fixture retains its synthetic/optional-file self-test and event/diagnostic CLI. Added contracts cover rate bounds, copied file lifetime, malformed load/error recovery, incremental seek chunking and prefetched position, pause/resume, cached mute, snapshot bounds/purity/lifetime, observer capacities/clear/overflow, independent instances and zero callback C++ allocation/free. Its per-instance core size was 204,624 bytes, including fixed observer storage. The synthetic observer test recorded 16 retained events and 17,596 overflowed events; original and adapted fixture hashes are recorded in `native/reference/SOURCES.json`.
- The original application's unchanged `scripts/check_native_extra_spc.mjs --fixture ...` passed 252 comparisons/2,064,384 stereo frames against the actual deployed SPC Worklet and shipped WASM. Twenty-eight scenarios at 44,100, 48,000 and 96,000 Hz used one-frame, 128-frame and irregular output partitions; every PCM value matched exactly. The checker also matched 810 snapshots' native/base/output frame counters, playing/mute fields, 64 KiB RAM hashes and all 128 DSP registers, plus ordered clock/register/value event sequences and overflow counts. It does not compare complete internal CPU state or establish a portable checkpoint. The reference inputs are optional validation dependencies, not SDK build dependencies; no device, IPC, UI, sanitizer, other-platform compiler or playback-deadline result is claimed.
- Temporary consumers included all twenty-three public headers and linked all eighteen ordinary static archives in forward and reverse order. Both produced identical finite, nonzero PCM with no missing or duplicate symbols; the previous seventeen libraries' output energies were unchanged. SNES and SPC each contain the same pinned accurate-DSP member, extracted once during ordinary static linking. This does not establish support for forcibly loading every member from every archive.
- `tetorica_spc_wav` creates an original SPC file in memory: SPC700 code drives timed DSP register/KON/KOFF writes, with original 64-sample BRR sine/triangle/pulse data. The host loads/plays/renders rather than scheduling individual notes. Actual CMake rendering produced 144,000 frames of 48 kHz stereo PCM16 with channel peaks approximately 0.183, no clipping, zero endpoints and a silent final 100 ms. Independent analysis matched all ten melody fundamentals within 0.25 cent and confirmed deliberate alternating stereo balance. The generated file and music require no external assets or complete IPL; fixed output gain/fades are example headroom, not Mixer defaults or hardware calibration.

The note intervals were approximately 200 ms and gates approximately 160 ms; the final release occurred at 2.700022 seconds. This checks that timing comes from the emulated SPC700/timer rather than host-side note scheduling.

real-device listening and hard real-time deadlines are separate checks. Existing
WASM source recipes and the previously compiled YM2612 artifact are unchanged.

The first SDK 0.1.1 matrix run, `40174420834`, exposed a test-only portability
failure on Linux x64 and ARM64: the allocation macros were active while
libstdc++'s `<stdlib.h>` declared its `using std::malloc/free` forwards. The
production library compiled; the instrumented test object failed. A small
test-only `nuked_audit.cpp` now includes `<stdlib.h>` before the unchanged Native
wrapper, keeping the standard declarations outside the audit macros. The
production source selection, vendor/core bytes and exported APIs are unchanged.
Local Release rebuild and all twenty-four CTest entries pass with this shim;
the corrected multi-platform run is recorded separately after completion.
